questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: They protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
They protect drivers' heads when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: They protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board protects a driver from moving cargo if the truck crashes or stops suddenly.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver crash ahead of you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: Stop a safe distance from the crash scene. Wait for police to arrive and tell them what you saw about the aggressive driving.

questions.question: When checking under your vehicle for leaks, you should look for all of these EXCEPT:
questions.correctAnswerText: Windshield wiper fluid
questions.explanation: Check under your vehicle for oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks before starting a trip.

questions.question: When should you use your headlights on high beam?

options.text: They are not needed when driving at night.
They give better light than the sun.
You should use high beams whenever it is safe and legal.
You should always use high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should use high beams whenever it is safe and legal.
questions.explanation: Use high beams at night when safe and legal for better visibility. Switch to low beams when within 500 feet of another vehicle to avoid blinding other drivers.

questions.question: In very hot weather, what may you need to do?

options.text: Speed up to cool the engine.
Slow down to prevent the engine from overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to prevent the engine from overheating.
questions.explanation: Faster speeds create more heat in the engine and tires. Slow down in very hot weather to avoid overheating.

questions.question: Which reason could result in being denied a hazmat endorsement?

options.text: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) considers you a security threat.
You are a lawful U.S. citizen.
You work for a foreign company.
You do not have perfect vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) considers you a security threat.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazmat endorsement if the TSA considers you a security threat, or if you renounce your citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, are convicted of certain felonies, or are judged mentally defective.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear and use engine braking.
Keep downshifting instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On steep downhill grades, use engine braking to control your speed. Use the brakes only to help with engine braking.

questions.question: Why is backing up with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot go in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Only back up if absolutely necessary.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail because of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of pressure.
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes fail when pressure is lost. They can also fade from overuse on long downgrades.

questions.question: When inspecting your engine, which should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drain the brake fluid.
questions.explanation: During engine inspection, check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level. Do not drain brake fluid.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure your glasses are clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear sunglasses.
questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses when driving at night. They reduce your vision. If you wear glasses, keep them clean. Be rested and alert before night driving.

questions.question: When driving a commercial vehicle across state lines, which law applies?

options.text: The law of the state where the trip started.
The law of the state the vehicle is in.
Federal regulations that override all state laws.
The driver can choose which state's laws to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The law of the state the vehicle is in.
questions.explanation: Follow the laws of the state you are driving in. Weight limits, cargo rules, and load covering rules vary by state. You must know the rules for each state where you drive.

questions.question: If brakes get too hot, what can happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may not work.
questions.explanation: If brakes get too hot, they can fade and lose stopping power. Do not rely only on brakes. Also use engine braking to slow down.

questions.question: If your driving test route has no railroad crossing, what happens?

options.text: You don't need to know anything about railroad crossings.
You may need to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
You must take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may need to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the proper way to cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: How long is a CDL valid?
questions.correctAnswerText: Five years
questions.explanation: A CDL is valid for five years from the date it is issued.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It is not available for air brakes.
It is not helpful in most driving situations.
It helps you stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS works with air brakes and helps prevent wheel lockup. This keeps you in control of your vehicle when braking.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: The parking brake in newer air brake vehicles is controlled by a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull it out to set the parking brake. Push it in to release it.

questions.question: Shaded areas of the road are dangerous because:

options.text: They have no moisture so they can't freeze.
They stay icy after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stay icy after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas stay cooler because they get less sunlight. Ice in shady spots takes longer to melt. These areas can be slippery after ice has melted elsewhere.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, air brakes start working:

options.text: Only when it is warm outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay.
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is a delay of at least half a second between when you press the pedal and when the brakes start working.

questions.question: Hauling hanging meat in a trailer is difficult because:

options.text: It should be avoided during summer.
Animals are attracted to the smell.
The load has a high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: The load has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable. It has a high center of gravity and swings as you drive. This makes the load unpredictable and harder to control.

questions.question: Which surface is the most slippery?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when it gets warm enough to slightly melt the ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use one set of turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers if you park on the side of the road. This is very important at night.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment in a vehicle required?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required.
questions.explanation: You must check for emergency equipment during a pre-trip inspection. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: A 40-foot load needs a minimum of how many tie-downs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. No matter the cargo size, use at least two tie-downs minimum.

questions.question: Why do dry bulk tanks require special care?

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and their loads often shift while traveling. Be extra careful on turns and curves.

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Get both sets of wheels onto the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.
questions.explanation: Stay on the shoulder until you stop, then signal and check your mirrors before returning to traffic. Do not brake hard at speeds over 20 mph on the shoulder. Keep one set of wheels on the pavement if possible.

questions.question: How do states verify that a CDL or CLP driver has only one license?

options.text: By using a computerized system that links all states.
By looking through the driver's wallet.

questions.correctAnswerText: By using a computerized system that links all states.
questions.explanation: All U.S. states share CDL and CLP information in a computerized database. When you apply for a license, the state checks this database to confirm you do not already have one in another state.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating found?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a set pressure. This information is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of driver fatigue?
questions.correctAnswerText: Feeling hungry
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, wandering thoughts, not remembering miles driven, missing exits, trouble holding head up, drifting lanes, following too closely, hitting shoulder rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates a switch that:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light.
Turns off the low pressure warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turns on the brake lights.
questions.explanation: In air brake systems, pressing the brake pedal sends air pressure to an electric switch, which turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles transporting hazardous materials.
Help drivers see a larger area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers see a larger area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles have curved, convex mirrors. These mirrors let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Why should you be cautious around a stopped bus?

options.text: It is not a concern if passengers are not getting off.
It should not be on the roadway.
You should be cautious whether or not you see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should be cautious whether or not you see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind the bus. The bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: What must you do if a load is over-length?

options.text: Put a warning flag on the end of the load.
Transport it only between 6 p.m. and 3 a.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put a warning flag on the end of the load.
questions.explanation: You may need special equipment, like warning flags or flashing lights, for an over-length load. You will need to get a permit. Driving is often limited to certain times.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Brake shoes with oil or grease on them
Brake pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: Check for these brake problems: cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: What happens when weight is loaded too high on a vehicle?

options.text: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
Items are more likely to fall down.
It is harder to unload the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity increases the risk that a vehicle will tip over. Load cargo with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: What is the danger of a cardboard box on the roadway?

options.text: It should be expected to be on the roadway.
It is usually empty and safe.
It could hold a heavy object that damages vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It could hold a heavy object that damages vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road can be dangerous. A cardboard box that seems harmless could contain a hard or heavy object that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day
questions.explanation: If your air brake system has manually operated drains, drain the tanks at the end of each day you drive.

questions.question: Which person should drivers NOT be worried about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people who are not watching the road. Watch out for road workers, drivers talking to passengers, and children near the road.

questions.question: What is the minimum tire tread depth for non-front tires on a commercial vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles need a tread depth of 4/32 of an inch in every major groove on front tires and 2/32 of an inch on other tires for safe operation.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may stop working.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often lets air out faster than the compressor can replace it. Air brakes may stop working if the pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Which surface has the least traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving on melting ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: Strong winds are most dangerous for which vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Heavier vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control your vehicle. Lighter vehicles have more trouble with strong winds.

questions.question: During a steering box inspection, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely mounted.
Check that the steering box has no leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Check for power steering fluid leaks and damage to hoses.

questions.question: When stopping your vehicle, how should you use the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it down repeatedly, not continuously.
Use the same amount of force each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually every time you slow or stop. The brake pressure you need depends on your speed and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Cancel the turn signal after completing the turn.
Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is completed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is completed.
questions.explanation: Signal early before turning or changing lanes. Keep the signal on while you complete the turn or lane change. Turn it off so you don't confuse other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do about broken suspension parts?

options.text: Repair them, but not right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Repair them right away.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up your vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Suspension problems are very dangerous and must be fixed immediately.

questions.question: Is texting while driving a CMV legal?
questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous. It is illegal to text while operating a CMV.

questions.question: What happens if you have more than one driver's license?

options.text: You are unlikely to be caught.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be penalized.
questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one driver's license. Breaking this law can result in jail time and/or a fine up to $5,000.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Switch to a low gear.
questions.explanation: Switch to a low gear before going down a hill. Gravity will speed up your vehicle as you go downhill.

questions.question: When can an applicant be denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: If they are a U.S. citizen.
If they are wanted for a misdemeanor.
If they are wanted for certain felonies.
If they already have a driver's license.

questions.correctAnswerText: If they are wanted for certain felonies.
questions.explanation: Your hazardous materials endorsement can be denied or canceled if you lack legal permanent status in the U.S., renounce U.S. citizenship, are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies, are judged mentally incompetent or committed to a mental institution, or are deemed a security threat.
